title: CI/CD commitment catalog and signing timeline (prototype)
body:
Purpose:
Iterate on a compact, operationally useful catalog of commit types, artifact signing timelines, and CI/CD expectations for Private deployments (VPC + on-prem). This is a working prototype: goal is to converge on a short contract that platform-operator teams and customers can rely on during upgrades and emergency rollbacks.

Scope:
- Helm charts used by private-deploy operator and umbrella charts
- Terraform modules that drive cluster bootstrap, networking, KMS integration, and image promotion controls
- GitOps/Argo workflows that reconcile customer clusters
- Image signing and attestation (cosign/attestations) and promotion timelines
- Canary/rollback decision gates and smoke checks

Assumptions & constraints (short):
- Private deploys may be air-gapped or VPC-isolated; not all clusters can reach public registries in real-time.
- Operators expect non-disruptive minor patches and an agreed minimal outage window for major upgrades.
- Customers may require NIST-compliant signing or HSM-backed KMS; timeline must accommodate enterprise procurement.

High-level commitment catalog (prototype):
- commit/type: infra-patch (patch release affecting infra tooling, non-breaking)
  - expected ring/time: propagate to internal staging within 2 hours, to customer-staging in 24h, to production in 72h (by default)
  - signing: short-form cosign signature on image + attestation, cosigned by release-service account
  - terraform impact: should not change module inputs required by existing state (safe by default)

- commit/type: chart-minor (non-breaking helm chart values or chart patch)
  - expected ring/time: canary on 1 customer cluster (opt-in) within 6h, global after 48h if no regression
  - signing: helm-chart metadata signed, image signatures required for new images
  - preflight: chart-version validation, values-compatibility check run against pinned values matrix

- commit/type: module-interface-change (TF module API changes)
  - expected ring/time: manual rollout, multi-day review window, migration plan required
  - signing: module artifacts in registry + change log + migration test harness
  - migration: provide tfstate-migration script and verified plan output in PR

- commit/type: major-operator-upgrade (breaking)
  - expected ring/time: 2-week canary + staged rollout; require customer sign-off for production schedule
  - signing: HSM-backed signing optional; policy requires attestations stored in customer provenance bucket
  - rollback: explicit backout plan, documented command sequence for operator version pinned rollback

Terraform module notes (practical):
- module contract principle: input schema MUST be additive. Deprecations must be supported for at least two releases (semver minor).
- publishable module artifacts: all modules must produce a short SHA lockfile and a versioned release tag on the module registry. The lockfile is committed alongside the operator bundle.
- terraform plan gating: CI must run plan and post a single-json plan artifact to GitHub PR. The plan artifact is required for on-prem approval.
- tfstate handling: never allow automated state migrations without human approval for private deploys. Provide a dry-run move script: scripts/tfstate-dryrun.sh that prints proposed state diffs.

Helm chart & values compatibility matrix (notes/draft approach):
- maintain a small compatibility matrix in repo: charts/compat-matrix.csv (chart, supported-operator-versions, deprecated-values)
- CI check: new chart PRs run a compatibility validator that warns on removed values and auto-generates a migration snippet.
- umbrella chart pinning: operator helm-install should pin child charts by exact chart digest (not floating semver) for production bundles. For canaries, allow semver-range but record resolved digest.
- values shrinkwrap idea: generate a "values.lock" for each release that records flattened values used in the canary/staging run. This file lives in the release tag.

Image signing & provenance timeline (prototype):
- build -> sign -> attest -> promote flow. Cosign is our standard for signatures; in addition, supply OCI attestation that includes: git-sha, build-job-id, tf-plan-id (if infra-affecting), and resolved chart-digest.
- promotion windows: images built in CI: signed within 15m and available in staging registry within 30m. Promotion to customer registry: by default within 4h, but may be longer for air-gapped customers depending on transport schedule.
- signing key rotation: all release keys rotate on a 90-day cadence. For HSM-backed keys used by enterprise customers, rotation schedule must be coordinated and documented in the customer onboarding repo.

GitOps/Argo pattern specifics (operational guidance):
- deploy branches: use release/* branches for staged rollouts. Argo apps point to specific release/* tag (or exact manifest commit).
- automated promotion: a promotion job (action) should create a new Argo app image override with the resolved digests and then update the app's target commit. Avoid pushing floating tags into Argo app spec.
- health checks: add a lightweight, fast path smokecheck for each chart that validates runtime readiness (not full e2e) — e.g., API responds to /healthz within 5s and token introspection works. Smokechecks live in release-tests/smokechecks and are invoked by Argo Rollout pre/post hooks.

Canary and rollback decision gates (operator-focused):
- telemetry + guard rails: define at least 4 signals for automated rollback decisions: median-latency delta, 5xx-rate, error-rate on critical endpoints, and token-use anomalies.
- rollout policy (prototype): 5% cluster weight for 30 minutes -> 25% for 2h -> 100% for 48h. If any signal crosses threshold at a stage, immediately pause progression and run rollback.
- emergency rollback command: make rollback a single operator command that sets Helm release to previous pinned digest and triggers Argo sync. Document in runbook exactly which secrets and tokens are required.

Preflight checklist for private deploy operator (short):
- PRs must include: plan artifact, cosign signature(s), values.lock if chart changes, migration script for tf module changes.
- Security review: if new third-party images are introduced, security must sign off OR the image must be added to allowlist and scanned.
- Network: verify customer registry connectivity or airgap transfer window scheduled.

Runbook excerpts (copyable commands):
- fetch last helm digest: 
  kubectl -n redwood get secret release-<name> -o jsonpath='{.data.release}' | base64 -d | jq -r '.chart.digests[0]'
- force rollback override: 
  argocd app set <app> --revision <commit-or-tag> && argocd app sync <app> --prune
- verify cosign signature: 
  cosign verify --key k8s://projects/mykeyring/cryptoKey/releases <registry>/<image>@sha256:<digest>

Open questions & TODOs (by owner):
- [Omar] finalize tf module lockfile format (ENGDEPLOY-456) — decide between single-line lockfile vs JSON metadata.
- [Maya] prototype values.lock generator and push a minimal PoC that flattens used values for operator bundles. (github PR linked above).
- [Ravi] propose a shortform smokecheck library (go/python) that is fast to run as Argo prehook.
- [Leah] draft customer-facing one-pager summarizing promotion windows and signing guarantees for onboarding.

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- land PR that enforces plan artifact gating for terraform modules (owner: Omar)
- add values.lock generator into helm-charts CI and validate in canary release pipeline (owner: Maya)
- update runbook with exact cosign key rotation steps and emergency contact (owner: Leah)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- consider storing a minimal attestation bundle per release in a customer-specified provenance bucket (helps audits).
- maybe expose a short API that returns current pinned digests for a customer cluster (useful for incident response).
- think about a simple "airgap manifest bundle" format that includes all resolved digests + attestations and a transport checklist.

Contact channels: #eng-private-deploy (Slack), pager rota: oncall-private-deploy.

This doc is intentionally terse — aim to iterate quickly. If you are reviewing, add inline comments or create PRs for any section you want hardened.
